summary.short: Requires developers that train foundation models with more than 10^26 operations to publish transparency reports and report critical safety incidents to California's Office of Emergency Services; those with over $500 million revenue must also publish and follow frontier AI frameworks. Adds whistleblower protections, preempts later local rules and plans CalCompute.
summary.long: SB 53 enacts the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act. A frontier model is a foundation model trained with more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, counting fine-tuning and later modifications; a large frontier developer also has, with affiliates, annual gross revenues above $500 million. Large frontier developers must write, implement, follow and publish a frontier AI framework on catastrophic risk, review it yearly, and send the Office of Emergency Services (OES) quarterly summaries of internal-use risk assessments. All frontier developers must publish a transparency report when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, report critical safety incidents to OES within 15 days (24 hours to an appropriate authority for imminent risk), and avoid materially false or misleading statements. Meeting an OES-designated federal standard can count as incident-reporting compliance. Large frontier developers face civil penalties of up to $1 million per violation, recoverable only by the Attorney General. Labor Code Chapter 5.1 protects covered employees who report catastrophic risks or violations, with injunctive relief and attorney's fees. A Government Operations Agency consortium is to design CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster, once funds are appropriated. Local frontier-AI rules adopted from 2025 are preempted.

territorial_scope.description: California statute. The definitions of frontier developer and large frontier developer state no territorial nexus (no in-state presence, sales or users requirement); within California it preempts local rules on frontier developers' management of catastrophic risk.

thresholds.value_text: greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations
thresholds.measurement: Includes computing for the original training run and any subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning or other material modifications the developer applies to a preceding foundation model (22757.11(i)(2)). Not indexed; the Department of Technology must recommend annually whether to update the definition (22757.14), with no automatic update.
thresholds.consequence: A foundation model is a 'frontier model', bringing the transparency-report, incident-reporting and statement duties into play
thresholds.conditions: The model must be a foundation model (broad data set, generality of output, adaptable to many tasks)

evidence.quote: “Frontier model” means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations.

thresholds.variable_text: computing power to train the frontier model
thresholds.value_text: at least as much computing power to train the frontier model as would meet the technical specifications found in subdivision (i)
thresholds.measurement: Compute the person has used or intends to use to train the model, by reference to the 10^26 specification in 22757.11(i); covers persons who have trained or initiated training
thresholds.consequence: The person is a 'frontier developer', the addressee of the chapter's developer duties and of the Labor Code whistleblower provisions

evidence.quote: “Frontier developer” means a person who has trained, or initiated the training of, a frontier model, with respect to which the person has used, or intends to use, at least as much computing power to train the frontier model as would meet the technical specifications found in subdivision (i).

thresholds.value_text: in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000)
thresholds.measurement: Annual gross revenues of the frontier developer together with its affiliates, collectively, in the preceding calendar year. Not indexed; subject to annual Department of Technology recommendations (22757.14(a)(3)), with no automatic update.
thresholds.consequence: A frontier developer is a 'large frontier developer': frontier AI framework, internal-use risk summaries to OES, risk-assessment summaries in transparency reports, framework-statement prohibition, internal anonymous whistleblower process, and the civil penalty in 22757.15

evidence.quote: “Large frontier developer” means a frontier developer that together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year.

thresholds.variable_text: death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people

thresholds.conditions: Foreseeable and material risk that the frontier developer's development, storage, use or deployment of a frontier model materially contributes; exclusions in 22757.11(c)(2)

obligations.summary: Large frontier developers must write, implement, comply with and publish a frontier AI framework covering standards, capability thresholds, mitigations, deployment review, third-party assessment, updates, model-weight cybersecurity, incident response, internal governance and internal-use risk.

evidence.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework that applies to the large frontier developer’s frontier models

obligations.summary: Large frontier developers must review the framework at least yearly and publish any materially modified framework with a justification within 30 days.
obligations.conditional_on: Large frontier developer; publication on material modification

evidence.quote: If a large frontier developer makes a material modification to its frontier AI framework, the large frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.

obligations.summary: Frontier developers must publish a transparency report (website, contact mechanism, release date, languages, output modalities, intended uses, use restrictions) before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model; a system or model card can satisfy this.
obligations.conditional_on: Deployment of a new or substantially modified frontier model

evidence.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report containing all of the following

obligations.summary: Large frontier developers must add to the transparency report summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments under their framework, their results, third-party evaluator involvement and other framework steps.
obligations.conditional_on: Large frontier developer; deployment of a new or substantially modified frontier model

evidence.quote: a large frontier developer shall include in the transparency report required by paragraph (1) summaries of all of the following

obligations.summary: Large frontier developers must send OES summaries of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use of their frontier models every three months or on another reasonable schedule communicated in writing.

evidence.quote: frontier developer shall transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models

obligations.summary: Frontier developers must not make materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk from their frontier models or their management of it; good-faith reasonable statements are excepted.

evidence.quote: developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about catastrophic risk from its frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk.

obligations.summary: Large frontier developers must not make materially false or misleading statements about implementing or complying with their frontier AI framework; good-faith reasonable statements are excepted.

evidence.quote: A large frontier developer shall not make a materially false or misleading statement about its implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI framework.

obligations.summary: Frontier developers that redact published documents (for trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety, national security or legal compliance) must describe the character and justification of each redaction and keep the unredacted information for five years.
obligations.conditional_on: Redaction of a document published under 22757.12

evidence.quote: the frontier developer shall describe the character and justification of the redaction in any published version of the document to the extent permitted by the concerns that justify redaction and shall retain the unredacted information for five years

obligations.summary: Frontier developers must report any critical safety incident involving their frontier models to OES within 15 days of discovery; amended reports are allowed and reporting on non-frontier foundation models is encouraged.
obligations.conditional_on: Discovery of a critical safety incident

evidence.quote: frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident

evidence.quote: If a frontier developer discovers that a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority

obligations.conditional_on: OES designation regulation under 22757.13(h) and the developer's election

obligations.summary: Frontier developers must not adopt or enforce rules, policies or contracts that prevent covered employees from disclosing, or retaliate against them for disclosing, catastrophic-risk dangers or violations of the TFAIA to the Attorney General, federal authorities or internal authorities.

“Affiliate” means a person controlling, controlled by, or under common control with a specified person, directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries.

“Artificial intelligence model” means an engineered or machine-based system that varies in its level of autonomy and that can, for explicit or implicit objectives, infer from the input it receives how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments.

“Catastrophic risk” means a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer’s development, storage, use, or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people

definitions.term: Critical safety incident (Business and Professions Code)

evidence.quote: Unauthorized access to, modification of, or exfiltration of, the model weights of a frontier model that results in death or bodily injury.
“Deploy” means to make a frontier model available to a third party for use, modification, copying, or combination with other software.

“Foundation model” means an artificial intelligence model that is all of the following: (1) Trained on a broad data set. (2) Designed for generality of output. (3) Adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks.
“Frontier AI framework” means documented technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
“Frontier developer” means a person who has trained, or initiated the training of, a frontier model

The quantity of computing power described in paragraph (1) shall include computing for the original training run and for any subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or other material modifications the developer applies to a preceding foundation model.

“Large frontier developer” means a frontier developer that together with its affiliates collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars ($500,000,000) in the preceding calendar year.
“Model weight” means a numerical parameter in a frontier model that is adjusted through training and that helps determine how inputs are transformed into outputs.

notes: The office named in the text is 'Office of Emergency Services'; the full name in the entity row is outside knowledge, unverified. The civil penalty in 22757.15 applies only to large frontier developers; the text states no penalty for frontier developers below the revenue threshold for the transparency-report, incident-reporting or false-statement duties. The civil penalty is coded administrative_fine although it is recovered by the Attorney General in a civil action, not imposed administratively. The text names no territorial nexus for frontier developers. Left open for the resolve stage: (1) effective date of Sections 2 and 4, which the text does not state (no urgency or operative-date clause); (2) whether and when the CalCompute appropriation was made (Gov. Code 11546.8 is inoperative until then); (3) any OES regulation designating federal standards under 22757.13(h); (4) the Legislative Counsel's Digest describes existing law requiring generative AI training-data documentation (likely us-ca-ab2013-2024), but the enacted sections do not reference it, so no relation is coded. Chapter number and approval date come from the raw page header (external evidence); the registry record's note that the chapter number came from memory is now matched by the raw leginfo header (Chapter 138).
